Subject: CloudScope: temporary launch accommodation request (Private Connect delay)

Team —

Quick summary: CloudScope (pilot customer, expected production launch 11/15) told us this morning that their cloud infra team has delayed enabling VPC Private Connect for two more weeks. Separately, they flagged that our long-sequence quantization/shim that was meant to land in the 11/10 runtime build is slipping and that combination materially increases their latency/cost risk for launch.

They've asked for a short-term commercial accommodation to keep the launch on track: specifically, a temporary usage credit or discounted rate covering the first ~3 months of production while we deliver the missing runtime pieces. They estimate the delta exposure at ~$35–45k.

Attachments: CloudScope_SOW_v2.pdf (SOW + payment schedule); initial procurement note from CloudScope (see convo below).

Ask: can we approve a one-off concession up to $50k (flexible structure: one-time credit or tiered rebate) conditioned on:
- CloudScope signs the attached SOW (same ARR baseline)
- a product milestone commit from us (ETA for long-seq shim) and an internal postmortem on what led to the slip

If we can't approve at that level, what's the max we can do quickly? Logan — can you run the economics and propose a structure (credit vs rebate) and potential revenue-protection language? Laura — need exec sign-off to proceed; can you weigh in with approval cadence?

Need an answer by COB Mon 11/2 to keep the customer on schedule.

Thanks,
Sofia Ivanova
Sr. Account Director | Redwood Inference

Sofia — thanks for the heads up.

Quick product context: the \"long-seq shim\" (KV cache allocation + quant-friendly attention path) was scoped to land in the 11/10 runtime and our engineering ETA pushed due to an infra dependency with our kernel scheduler. The fix itself is low-risk and on the critical path but requires a short testing window; our internal ETA is now ~11/20.

Options I see:
- Credit only (commercial fix) — fastest from a go/no-go standpoint, but doesn't guarantee they stay on the platform if latency/cost is worse than expected.
- Product commitment + milestone + smaller credit — we offer public milestone dates and a small credit (eg $20–30k) to compensate while shipping the runtime fix; gives them visibility.
- Temporary feature toggle (experimental prefix caching tuned to CloudScope) — we can enable a controlled knob for them to reduce tokens/cost, but this requires SRE time to support at launch.

If Finance prefers a smaller dollar amount, I'd push for the product-commit + $25k credit + the temporary toggle as a package — gives CloudScope coverage while protecting our economics. Attaching a short release plan excerpt.

Maya
Maya Srinivasan
Product Lead, Serving Runtime

All — ran quick numbers based on their projected 3-month volume in the SOW:

- Expected invoice baseline (3 months): $180k
- Customer ask range (from Sofia): $35k–45k (19–25% of 3-month ARR)

Concession structures to consider (rough):
1) One-time credit of $40k applied to first invoice — simple, immediate relief, hits revenue recognition as a discount.
2) Usage rebate: 30% off over first two invoices capped at $40k — spreads impact but operationally heavier.
3) Conditional credit: $30k credit + milestone clause (if we miss 11/20, additional $15k credit) — shares risk.

From a finance/io perspective I prefer option (3) — limits our immediate exposure and ties extra payout to a clear product miss. If legal/procurement want a rebate, we'll need explicit metric gating and an SLO in the SOW.

Attached: ConcessionCalc_CloudScope.xlsx (workbook with scenario math).

Logan
Revenue Operations

Team —

I reviewed the situation and the scenarios Logan laid out. We will approve a conditional commercial accommodation to preserve the launch and protect the account. Final decision below:

Decision:
- Approve a $30,000 one-time credit applied to CloudScope's first invoice.
- Add a conditional clause: if Redwood misses the 11/20 product milestone for the long-seq shim, an additional $15,000 credit will be applied automatically (no further exec approval required).
- Require CloudScope to sign the attached SOW and agree to a 12-month commitment at the baseline ARR in the SOW.
- Offer a dedicated SRE contact for first two weeks of production (hours capped, escalation plan in SOW).

Conditions / Next steps:
1) Karthik: have procurement sign the SOW and get DocuSign by 11/6. Use the HubSpot deal above and tag legal for an amended SOW that includes the conditional credit language.
2) Logan: prepare the discount accounting note and update revenue recognition docs so the team knows how to book the concession.
3) Maya: confirm the 11/20 milestone in writing and assign an engineering owner for the dedicated SRE support.

If any of the above items cannot be met, we will revisit the amount. I do not want open-ended credits beyond the conditional structure above.
